## Natural history notes

A sprawling or climbing cactus characterized by long, slender ribbed stems with small spines and exceptionally large, fragrant white flowers that open primarily at night. Princess of the Night may grow as an epiphyte or scramble through surrounding vegetation, with stems extending several meters through shrubs and trees. It is native from eastern Mexico and Belize through parts of the northern Caribbean but is introduced in Florida, where established populations occur particularly in southern Florida along hammock edges, roadsides, and other warm subtropical habitats. Its nocturnal flowers are adapted to night-active pollinators, and flowering is followed by rounded fleshy fruits.
